== Biography ==
===First Marriage to Phillips===


Andrew Alexander married first a dau. of Sir Thomas Phillips, called Governor Phillips, and had a son and heir, Jacob Alexander.  <ref name="burkeland"/> 

Andrew's first wife, a Miss Phillips, was a relative of the Alexanders<ref name="wikical"/>

===Second Marriage to Hilles===

Andrew Alexander married secondly a dau. of the Laird of Hilles, and had a son, John Alexander . . ."<ref name="burkeland"/> 

Andrew's second wife was a Miss Hillhouse<ref name="wikical"/>

===1663 Grant of Lands===

Captain Andrew Alexander of Errigal, County Donegal, forbearer of the Earls of Caledon, was granted lands at Ballyclose near Limavady, County Londonderry in 1663.  <ref name="wikical"> [[Wikipedia: Earl of Caledon]] Accesssed October 30, 2018 [[Day=1904|jhd]] </ref>

===1689 Attainted===

Andrew Alexander was attainted by James II in 1689.  <ref name="burkeland"> Burke's Landed Gentry (1894), p. 16 </ref>

Andrew Alexander was later attainted by the parliament called by James II in Dublin in 1689. <ref name="wikical"/>

===Children===

#Jacob Alexander, son of Andrew and his first wife.  Jacob was the ancestor of the Alexanders of Ahilly (Donegal).<ref name="wikical"/>
#John Alexander, son of Andrew and his second wife, married Anne White, daughter of John White, of Cadyhill, County Londonderry, and had four children, of whom the first, Nathaniel Alexander was born in 1689 and became an Alderman of the city of Derry in 1755 and died on 22 September 1761, having had with other children a third son, James Alexander, who became the 1st Earl of Caledon.<ref name="wikical"/>

== Research Notes ==
===1800 Earls of Caledon===

The title Earl of Caledon in the Peerage of Ireland was created 29 December 1800 by George III.  The first holder was James Alexander, 1st Viscount Caledon.  The seat of the barony is Caledon Castle in County Tyrone.  

James Alexander was a merchant who had made an enormous fortune in India. He also represented the constituency of Londonderry City in the Irish House of Commons. Alexander had already been created Baron Caledon in 1790[2] and Viscount Caledon, of Caledon in the County of Tyrone, in 1797,[3] also in the Peerage of Ireland.

James Alexander was succeeded by his son, the second Earl. He was the first Governor of the Cape Colony and sat in the House of Lords as an Irish Representative Peer from 1804 to 1839. His son, the third Earl, briefly represented County Tyrone in the House of Commons as a Tory and was an Irish Representative Peer between 1841 and 1855. His eldest son, the fourth Earl, sat in the House of Lords as an Irish Representative Peer from 1877 to 1898. He was succeeded by his eldest son, the fifth Earl. He never married and was succeeded by his nephew, the 6th Earl. He was the son of the Hon. Herbrand Charles Alexander, second son of the fourth Earl. Today the titles are held by his only son, the seventh Earl, who succeeded in 1980. Lord Caledon was made Lord Lieutenant of County Armagh in 1989.

A possible identification concerns Andrew Allexander. The banns/marriage index records Joannet Glasgow and Andrew Allexander/ on 8 August 1661 at Glasgow.<ref>Scotland’s People: Old Parish Registers — banns and marriages: OPR 644 / 1/230 / 230; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ record].</ref> The original parish register image has not been inspected. The combined index date does not by itself identify the precise event type. The identification remains uncertain.
